papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, expressibility section, experimental setup, hardware results text, ablation, conclusion; result tables are garbled in extraction and were not used
papers.what_it_is: A parameterized quantum circuit for image classification, built on pixel locality and IBM connectivity, tested with inference on ibm_kingston.

assertions.value: The authors report that on quantum hardware their DAQC circuit achieves performance competitive with strong classical baselines (ResNet-18/50, DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B0) and substantially outperforms Quantum Circuit Search baselines.
quotes: On quantum hardware, DAQC achieves performance competitive with strong classical baselines (e.g., ResNet-18/50, DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B0) and substantially outperforming Quantum Circuit Search (QCS) baselines.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, three image datasets, small circuits.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is on binary and 4-class tasks mainly; the paper itself says 10-class results trail the classical baselines.

assertions.value: The authors report that for MNIST-2 the hardware run on ibm_kingston with DD+TREX+Twir+ZNE gives AUC 0.9998 and ACC 0.985.
quotes: The hardware run on ibm_kingston with DD+TREX+Twir+ZNE preserves this near-saturation (AUC 0.9998, ACC 0.985, specificity 0.9899, sensitivity 0.9802, F1 0.9851) for MNIST-2
assertions.certainty_reason: Single binary task, 200 test samples on hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that the learned parameters were fixed and only inference was run on ibm_kingston, using 200 randomly selected test samples per dataset because of limited access.
quotes: For real hardware evaluation, we keep the learned parameters fixed and run inference on ibm_kingston.
we randomly selected 200 samples from the testing set for evaluation on the real device due to the limited access.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own statement of its hardware evaluation setup, Section 2.2.
assertions.reader_inference: Training was not done on hardware, so the hardware result tests inference under noise only.

assertions.value: The authors state that the design is limited to 16 qubits in this study due to hardware limits, and that on the harder 10-class tasks DAQC maintains high AUC (around 0.95).
quotes: we limit our DAQC design to 16 qubits in this study due to the limitations of current quantum hardware.
On the harder 10-class tasks, DAQC maintains high AUC (around 0.95), indicating that it can extract useful decision signals with few parameters and input constraints.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Complex Systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section III opening, conclusion; application sections skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A review of QML for complex systems: variational methods, neural-network quantum states, learning dynamics, applications and federated QML.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Review surveys foundational QML paradigms, including variational quantum algorithms, quantum kernel methods and neural-network quantum states, with emphasis on complex quantum systems.
quotes: We survey foundational QML paradigms, including variational quantum algorithms, quantum kernel methods, and neural-network quantum states, with emphasis on their applicability to complex quantum systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the Review's own scope.

assertions.value: The review reports, citing prior work, that many variational circuit architectures suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size or circuit depth, rendering training ineffective.
quotes: many variational circuit architectures suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size or circuit depth, rendering training ineffective
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited result, attributed to McClean et al.

assertions.value: The authors state that a deeper theoretical understanding of when and why quantum resources improve learning performance for complex systems is needed.
quotes: Equally important will be a deeper theoretical understanding of when and why quantum resources improve learning performance for complex systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' view of the state of the field.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Optimization Benchmark Suite for Airline Crew Pairing and More
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, architecture overview, results and summary; ACP modeling details skimmed
papers.what_it_is: An open-source software framework for variational quantum optimization experiments, demonstrated on airline crew pairing and MaxCut.

assertions.value: The authors state that they introduce a set of open-source packages forming an extensible framework for quantum optimization.
quotes: We introduce a set of open-source packages that form a highly extensible framework for quantum optimization.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states what the paper delivers.

assertions.value: The authors report an experiment on a small instance of the Airline Crew Pairing problem, using a genetic algorithm to optimize the parameters of the maQAOA ansatz, and show the most likely measured pairing in a figure.
quotes: We ran an experiment on a small instance of the ACP problem, constructed in the style described by Kasirzadeh et al. [28].
We used a genetic algorithm to optimize the parameters of the maQAOA ansatz.
assertions.certainty_reason: Demonstration on a small instance; no numbers in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The text gives no performance number; results are in figures and a table.

assertions.value: The authors state that, since the capabilities of quantum optimization algorithms are restricted by hardware, most use cases involve small problem instances.
quotes: Since the current capabilities of quantum optimization algorithms are restricted by the hardware, most use cases revolve around small problem instances.

papers.what_it_is: A mathematics paper on eigenvalue counting for Schrodinger operators on quantum star graphs (spectral theory, not quantum computing).
papers.why_not: Pure spectral theory of differential operators on metric graphs; no quantum computing or machine learning content.

papers.title_in_file: Bridging Quantum and Classical Computing in Drug Design: Architecture Principles for Improved Molecule Generation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract through conclusion, including limitations and hardware validation
papers.what_it_is: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization of a hybrid quantum-classical GAN for molecule generation on QM9, mostly simulated, with a 10-molecule hardware check.

assertions.value: The authors report that their optimized model achieves a 2.27-fold higher Drug Candidate Score than prior quantum-hybrid benchmarks and 2.21-fold higher than the classical baseline, while reducing parameter count by more than 60%.
quotes: achieving a 2.27-fold higher Drug Candidate Score (DCS) than prior quantum-hybrid benchmarks and 2.21-fold higher than the classical baseline, while reducing parameter count by more than 60%
assertions.certainty_reason: One study; baselines were re-implemented by the authors; simulator results.
assertions.reader_inference: The baselines are the authors' re-implementations, so the fold gains are relative to those.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best models consistently used multiple (3-4) shallow (4-8 qubit) quantum circuits layered sequentially, while the classical part showed less sensitivity above a minimum capacity.
quotes: Key findings favor layering multiple (3-4) shallow (4-8 qubit) quantum circuits sequentially, while classical architecture shows less sensitivity above a minimum capacity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from 100 optimization trials on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that primary results rely on idealized simulations lacking NISQ noise and topology constraints, and that a 10-molecule hardware batch is too small to permit definitive conclusions.
quotes: Simulation vs. Real Hardware: Primary results rely on idealized simulations lacking NISQ noise and topology constraints.
The small sample size (n = 10) and the inherent stochasticity of both GAN generation and NISQ hardware execution prevent definitive conclusions about performance parity
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 4.3 states the limitation; Section 3.8 repeats it for the hardware batch.

papers.title_in_file: On the Complementarity of Quantum and Classical Features: Adaptive Hybrid Quantum-Classical Feature Fusion for Breast Cancer Classification
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, implementation details, BUS-UCLM discussion, conclusion; other results tables not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A dual-branch hybrid quantum-classical feature-fusion model for breast cancer image classification, evaluated by classical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the TSHF fusion strategy, pairing a ResNet backbone with a trainable quantum circuit, reached a peak accuracy of 87.82%, F1-score of 91.77% and AUC-ROC of 89.08% on BreastMNIST.
quotes: achieved a peak accuracy of 87.82%, F1-score of 91.77%, and an AUC-ROC of 89.08%
assertions.certainty_reason: Peak figure from one dataset in simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: A peak value rather than a mean over runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that all quantum circuits were run in classical simulation and that the study is constrained by the limits of classical simulation, with hardware execution left as future work.
quotes: Quantum simulations were performed using the lightning.qubit backend
it is inherently constrained by the limits of classical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that BUS-UCLM is the most glaring limitation of feature fusion, and that near-zero learned temperature values show TSHF degrading to the stronger branch when one modality contributes nothing.
quotes: BUS-UCLM presents perhaps the most difficult scenario and the most glaring limitation of feature fusion.
has nothing useful to contribute and properly degrades to the stronger

papers.title_in_file: Comparison of Quantum Simulators for Variational Quantum Search: A Benchmark Study
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark of eight classical quantum-circuit simulators running a variational quantum search circuit.

assertions.value: The authors report that most simulators show exponential growth in time and memory with the number of qubits, except for Qulacs, and recommend Qulacs for memory and Pennylane with GPU for time.
quotes: Most simulators exhibit exponential growth in time and memory consumption with the number of qubits, except for Qulacs.
we recommend using Qulacs for optimal memory efficiency and Pennylane with GPU for optimal time efficiency.
assertions.certainty_reason: One benchmark on one machine and one circuit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the results calculate the exact expectation value without considering noise and sampling effects, and so validate algorithm correctness rather than hardware performance.
quotes: The results presented above focus on calculating the exact expectation value without considering noise and sampling effects.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV states the scope limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that variational quantum search has demonstrated exponential advantage over Grover's search algorithm and has been verified up to 26 input qubits (prior work by one of the authors).
quotes: has demonstrated exponential advantage over Grover
has been successfully verified up to 26 input qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to earlier work, not shown here.
